claims.text: Not one of the twelve counties has 69 percent of its jobs held by its own residents (H2, matrix callout, default verdict sentence, mobile matrix header).
claims.source: LEHD LODES8 origin-destination, Ohio 2022, segment JT00, main + aux
claims.actual: sorted(((r['work_name'], r['in_county']) for r in D['ls']['matrix']), key=lambda x: -x[1])[:3]
claims.falsified_if: Any county reaches 0.69. DENOMINATOR: the share is over ALL jobs worked in the county, including those held from outside PIC-12 — dividing by the PIC-12 interior alone inflates every share (Summit reads 53.9% that way against 48.4% correctly) and would break the claim this page makes.

claims.text: Summit County, the cluster's center, is at 48.4 percent (standfirst, hero card, matrix callout, diagonal figure title).
claims.source: LODES 2022, Summit work end, all home ends
claims.assert: abs([r for r in D['ls']['matrix'] if r['work_name']=='Summit'][0]['in_county'] - 0.484) < 0.003
claims.actual: [(r['work_name'], r['in_county'], r['jobs_total']) for r in D['ls']['matrix'] if r['work_name']=='Summit']
claims.falsified_if: LODES revises, or the footprint changes. Cross-checked: these shares reproduce the figures in the LODES codebook independently derived by another session, which is the only cross-session validation in the stack.

claims.text: Summit County holds 265,460 jobs (standfirst, hero card, diagonal note).
claims.source: LODES 2022, Summit work end, all home ends
claims.actual: [r['jobs_total'] for r in D['ls']['matrix'] if r['work_name']=='Summit']
claims.falsified_if: A LODES revision moves Summit's job count; the hand-typed 265,460 in the standfirst would then be stale.

claims.text: Ashtabula is the highest at 68.5 percent and Geauga the lowest at 30.8 percent, out of exactly twelve counties (hero cards, matrix callout, default verdict sentence).
claims.assert: (lambda rows: len(rows) == 12 and max(rows, key=lambda r: r['in_county'])['work_name'] == 'Ashtabula' and abs(max(r['in_county'] for r in rows) - 0.6848) < 0.003 and min(rows, key=lambda r: r['in_county'])['work_name'] == 'Geauga' and abs(min(r['in_county'] for r in rows) - 0.3083) < 0.003)(D['ls']['matrix'])
claims.actual: (max(((r['work_name'], r['in_county']) for r in D['ls']['matrix']), key=lambda x: x[1]), min(((r['work_name'], r['in_county']) for r in D['ls']['matrix']), key=lambda x: x[1]))
claims.falsified_if: A revision changes which county is the extreme, or moves either share off the value the cards and callouts print.

claims.text: Four counties are under half, and they are Summit, Medina, Portage and Geauga (generated H2, orange accent meaning, matrix figure subtitle, mobile annotation).
claims.assert: set(r['work_name'] for r in D['ls']['matrix'] if r['in_county'] < 0.5) == {'Summit', 'Medina', 'Portage', 'Geauga'}
claims.actual: sorted((r['work_name'], r['in_county']) for r in D['ls']['matrix'] if r['in_county'] < 0.5)
claims.falsified_if: A county crosses 0.5 in either direction. The orange accent means exactly 'under half' on this page, so a membership change must recolor the matrix outlines, the diagonal bars and the mobile list together.

claims.text: Each row accounts for every job in that county — twelve home counties plus an outside-footprint remainder (matrix figure subtitle: rows sum to 100%).
claims.source: derived: interior cells plus external inflow per work county
claims.assert: all(abs(sum(c['share'] for c in r['cells']) + r['outside_share'] - 1) < 0.003 for r in D['ls']['matrix'])
claims.actual: [(r['work_name'], round(sum(c['share'] for c in r['cells']) + r['outside_share'], 4)) for r in D['ls']['matrix'][:3]]
claims.falsified_if: Any row fails to sum to one. A matrix whose rows do not close is not a share matrix, and every cell would be reading against a different denominator.

claims.text: The distant-metro share is not a pandemic effect: Franklin County was already the largest external source in 2019.
claims.source: LODES 2019 baseline, pulled specifically to test this
claims.falsified_if: A revised 2019 vintage shows distant metros small. THIS CLAIM KILLED A STORY: the candidate 'remote work broke the labor shed' required Franklin to be small in 2019. It was 23,506 — already the largest. The hypothesis is dead and does not appear on this page; what survives is that adjacent and distant were always different things.

claims.text: Distant residence grew 13 percent from 2019 to 2022 while adjacent commuting grew 1 percent (external figure title, lede).
claims.source: LODES 2019 and 2022, adjacent vs distant totals
claims.falsified_if: Either growth rate leaves the band that rounds to the printed 13% and 1%. The figure title recomputes at render time, but the lede's 'roughly half' and the hero card lean on the same split.

claims.text: Franklin County (Columbus) is the largest single external source: 26,960 jobs in 2022, 23,506 in 2019 (vignette band, reading line).
claims.source: LODES 2019 and 2022, top external home counties
claims.assert: (lambda t: t[0]['name'].startswith('Franklin') and t[0]['jobs_2022'] == 26960 and t[0]['jobs_2019'] == 23506 and t[0]['jobs_2022'] == max(r['jobs_2022'] for r in t))(D['ls']['external']['top'])
claims.falsified_if: A revision reorders the top external sources or moves Franklin's counts; the hand-typed 26,960 and 23,506 in the vignette would then be stale, as would its 'About 27,000' headline.

claims.text: This is the whole economy, not the polymer cluster.
claims.source: LODES origin-destination carries no industry dimension at any grain
claims.falsified_if: Anyone describes these figures as the cluster's workforce. Industry detail exists only in the WAC workplace files, at 2-digit sectors, and cannot be crossed with residence. A polymer-specific version of this page cannot be built from this source.
claims.checked_by: Source-capability rule, not a data check

claims.text: In nine of the twelve counties, the share of jobs held locally exceeds the share of residents' jobs that stay local (reciprocal figure title).
claims.source: LEHD LODES8 2022, both directions per county
claims.assert: len([p for p in D['b']['pairs'] if p['work_own'] > p['res_own']]) == 9
claims.actual: sorted((p['name'], round(p['work_own'] - p['res_own'], 3)) for p in D['b']['pairs'])
claims.falsified_if: The count leaves nine. KNIFE EDGE: Mahoning's gap is -0.1 percentage points, so a small revision flips it to ten; the figure title is generated from this count, but the claim exists to force that regeneration to be noticed.

claims.text: Cuyahoga runs the other way: 58 percent of its jobs are filled locally while 76 percent of its residents' jobs stay local (reciprocal annotation).
claims.assert: (lambda p: abs(p['work_own'] - 0.5792) < 0.003 and abs(p['res_own'] - 0.7645) < 0.003)(one(p for p in D['b']['pairs'] if p['name'] == 'Cuyahoga'))
claims.actual: [(p['work_own'], p['res_own']) for p in D['b']['pairs'] if p['name'] == 'Cuyahoga']
claims.falsified_if: Either Cuyahoga share moves off the values the on-chart annotation rounds from (58% and 76%).

claims.text: 95 percent of counties in peer metropolitan areas are also below 69 percent, so the county-level pattern is not specific to Northeast Ohio (H2 'Ninety-five percent', reading line, closer).
claims.source: LEHD LODES8 2022, 397 counties in 73 single-state peer metros, in-state basis both sides
claims.falsified_if: The share leaves the band that rounds to 95 percent. TIGHTENED 2026-08-27: the old bound (> 0.90) allowed a value of 0.92 to pass while the H2 said 'Ninety-five percent'; the tolerance now guards the printed word, not just the direction. If this drops, the county-level framing becomes a regional finding again and the hero must change back.

claims.text: The median PIC-12 county sits 3.5 points above the peer median: 55.3 percent against 51.8 (benchmark bracket, reading line, closer).
claims.falsified_if: The gap leaves the band that rounds to 3.5 points, or the direction flips. TIGHTENED 2026-08-27: the claim previously guarded only the direction, while the page now draws a labeled bracket with the size of the gap.

claims.text: On the benchmark's in-state basis, Ashtabula reads 72.7 percent and crosses the 69 percent line (bench reading line).
claims.source: LEHD LODES8 2022, in-state basis both sides
claims.assert: (lambda r: abs(r['own_share_work'] - 0.7271) < 0.003)(one(r for r in D['b']['benchmark']['pic12_counties'] if r['name'] == 'Ashtabula'))
claims.actual: [(r['name'], r['own_share_work'], r['percentile']) for r in D['b']['benchmark']['pic12_counties'] if r['name'] == 'Ashtabula']
claims.falsified_if: Ashtabula's in-state share moves off 72.7 percent or drops below 0.69, which would delete the denominator lesson the reading line teaches.

claims.text: Just under 90 percent of the jobs in PIC-12 are held by people who live in PIC-12, and just under 90 percent of PIC-12 residents' jobs sit inside it.
claims.source: LEHD LODES8 2022; workplace side Ohio main+aux, resident side Ohio main plus six neighbor aux files
claims.falsified_if: Either share drops below 0.85. NOTE the two are different quantities with different denominators and are never summed or differenced; they agree here, which is a finding, not a construction.

claims.text: Among peer regions of six or more counties, only Pittsburgh holds as much of its workforce inside its own borders as PIC-12 (regions figure title, on-chart label 'the only peer that matches', closer).
claims.assert: sum(1 for r in D['b']['regions'] if r['kind'] != 'footprint' and r['region_share_work'] >= D['b']['totals']['work_region_share']) <= 1 and sum(1 for r in D['b']['regions'] if r['kind'] != 'footprint' and r['region_share_work'] >= D['b']['totals']['work_region_share'] and not r['name'].startswith('Pittsburgh')) == 0
claims.falsified_if: Two or more peer regions match or beat PIC-12, or the matching peer stops being Pittsburgh — the on-chart label names it. Region share rises with region size, so this is a bounded claim about comparable regions and NOT a national ranking. EXTENDED 2026-08-27: the assertion now also checks the matching peer's identity, since the label hand-names Pittsburgh.

claims.text: Only about 1 percent of PIC-12 residents' jobs are outside Ohio, so the resident-side figure is not hollowed out by out-of-state work.
claims.source: LEHD LODES8 2022, aux files for PA, WV, IN, KY, NY
claims.falsified_if: Out-of-state work exceeds 3 percent. Michigan's 2022 aux file is not published by LEHD, so this is a lower bound; MI is not adjacent to any PIC-12 county, which is why the omission is tolerable and stated.
